title: Soft fruit salad for little fingers
summary: Ripe, soft fruits cut small and safe: a colorful finger-food snack for pincer-grasp practice.
texture: Small pieces of very ripe, soft fruit that squash easily. Blueberries are smashed flat; no whole round fruit.
ingredients: 1/4 ripe banana, cut into small pieces
1/4 very ripe pear or mango, peeled and diced small
steps: Peel the pear or mango and cut everything into small, soft pieces about the size of a pea.
Smash each blueberry flat with a fork so it's no longer round.
Put a few pieces at a time on baby's tray rather than the whole pile.
choking: Whole blueberries, grapes and cherry tomatoes are round choking hazards: smash or quarter them lengthwise.
Skip hard fruit like raw apple. Grate it or steam it soft instead.
storage: Best fresh. Cut fruit keeps a few hours covered in the fridge.
tips: A few pieces at a time helps baby focus and stops them from overfilling their mouth.
Kiwi and ripe melon are great soft additions.
